name: comm-verify-browser-ui
description: Use when verifying application UI behavior or assessing browser-specific test fidelity; excludes harness validation.

# Verify browser behavior

Inputs: contract/reference, target, supported conditions, scenario and authority.
General test quality/TDD/check execution retain their existing owners.

1. Use a real browser for contracts depending on rendering, events, visibility,
   interaction, scrolling or responsiveness. Suitable lightweight tests can verify
   pure logic, not establish browser-dependent claims.
2. Establish needed conditions through comm-prepare-browser-check when unverified;
   reuse valid existing setup. Before choosing coverage read
   [browser coverage](references/coverage.md); before designing/reviewing relevant
   scenarios read [fidelity cases](references/fidelity.md).
3. Exercise the intended user path and assert its observable contract. Apply
   comm-assess-project-tests for general quality and comm-run-project-checks for
   general scope/execution; do not substitute passing narrow tests for coverage.
4. Compare appearance against approved intent through comm-preserve-visual-design.
   Tool choice remains with comm-choose-effective-solution; no fixed vendor or
   assumed installation.

Done: report actual contract evidence, environment/coverage and unverified cases.
Keep harness validation separate and use existing recording/evidence procedures.
comm-verify-browser-ui.references/fidelity.md:
# Browser-specific fidelity

Use cases relevant to the claim.

1. Textarea: model initial text/default value and current .value after edits,
   not a value attribute or permanently empty field.
2. Events: reproduce relevant dispatch lifetime; currentTarget becomes null after
   dispatch. Do not preserve it throughout an awaited fake handler or equate
   every await with dispatch completion. Exercise affected asynchronous paths.
3. Reachability: DOM element.click() does not prove user access. For pointer
   claims check visibility, scrolling, obstruction, intended target/allowed
   descendant and effect using suitable browser input; manual CDP coordinates
   are not mandatory.
4. Wiring: a helper unit test does not establish its UI call site. Use an
   interaction that reaches the real caller and observable result.
5. Measurement: execute the actual measurer. Lightweight tests may supply input
   geometry; browser-layout claims need real rendering. Stubbing the result hides
   defects in the measurer itself.
6. Containment: test content as well as container boundaries, including relevant
   overflow/clipping/scrolling and obstruction of neighboring controls. Judge
   against the contract; intentional popovers may extend beyond their parent.
comm-verify-browser-ui.references/coverage.md:
# Browser coverage

Use project support commitments and affected risks with the existing general
scope owner; do not invent a universal browser/device matrix.

Consider relevant engines/platforms/input modes; width AND height, responsive
transitions and orientations; supported themes and states such as open overlays,
long content, loading, refusal and restoration. Choose necessary combinations,
preserve mandatory checks, not every possible Cartesian combination. Actual
state verification belongs to comm-prepare-browser-check.

Identify actual browser/version/platform, sizes/states, real devices versus
emulation, and unverified support. Missing support requirements block broad
compatibility claims, not independent authorized checks. Distinguish application
behavior from observed platform-controlled interfaces.
